options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Venous system and portal systems of the frog
solution.explanation: NCERT: the veins collect blood from different parts of the body to the heart and form the venous system. Special venous connections are present between the liver and intestine as well as between the kidney and the lower parts of the body; the former is called the hepatic portal system and the latter the renal portal system.
steps: Statement II → false: kidney–lower body connection is the renal portal system
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept Statement II, which names the wrong portal system; B rejects Statement I, which is NCERT's description of the venous system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy – circulatory system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about reproduction in the frog are correct?

(a) Fertilisation is external and takes place in water.
(b) Development involves a larval stage called the tadpole.
(c) A mature female lays only a single ovum at a time.
(d) In the male, the testes are attached to the upper part of the kidneys by the mesorchium.
(e) In the female, the oviducts open into the urinogenital duct of the kidneys.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: fertilisation is external and takes place in water; development involves a larval stage called the tadpole, which undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. The testes adhere to the upper part of the kidneys by the mesorchium. In the female, the ovaries have no functional connection with the kidneys, and the oviducts open into the cloaca separately.
steps: (e) false – oviducts open into the cloaca separately
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D include (e); C and D include (c); C also leaves out external fertilisation (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy – reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Suppose both ureters of a male frog and of a female frog were tied off just after they leave the kidneys. Release of which of the following to the exterior would be blocked?

options.text: Urine in the male only; gametes in both frogs
Urine in both frogs; gametes in neither frog
Urine in both frogs; sperms in the male, but not ova in the female
Urine in the female only; gametes in the male only

solution.concept: Urinogenital ducts of male and female frogs
solution.explanation: NCERT: in male frogs the ureters act as urinogenital ducts – the vasa efferentia open into Bidder's canal in the kidney, which communicates with the urinogenital duct coming out of the kidney. In the female, the ovaries have no functional connection with the kidneys and the oviducts open into the cloaca separately. Tying the ureters therefore blocks urine in both sexes, and sperms in the male, but the ova of the female still leave through the oviducts.
steps: Male: ureter = urinogenital duct → urine + sperms blocked
Female: ureter carries urine only; oviducts separate → ova still released
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D forget that both frogs' ureters carry urine; A also blocks ova; B forgets that the male's sperms travel through the urinogenital duct.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', frog: anatomy – reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Urine in both frogs; sperms in the male, but not ova in the female

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
A tissue has cells enclosed in small cavities within a solid and pliable matrix that resists compression. Which of the following statements about this tissue are correct?

(a) It is cartilage, a specialised connective tissue.
(b) In adults, it is present at the tip of the nose, the outer ear joints and between adjacent bones of the vertebral column.
(c) Its ground substance is hard, non-pliable and rich in calcium salts.
(d) Its cells secrete the matrix that surrounds them.
(e) In vertebrate embryos, most of this tissue is later replaced by bone in the adult.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A solid, pliable matrix that resists compression is NCERT's description of cartilage. Its cells (chondrocytes) are enclosed in small cavities within the matrix secreted by them. In adults cartilage is present in the tip of the nose, outer ear joints, between adjacent bones of the vertebral column, limbs and hands. Most of the cartilages in vertebrate embryos are replaced by bones in adults. A hard, non-pliable matrix rich in calcium salts describes bone.
solution.why_others_wrong: B and C include (c), the bone matrix; A leaves out the embryonic replacement by bone (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Structural Organisation in Animals', animal tissue – specialised connective tissue

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Suppose the cilia of the epithelium lining a person's bronchioles stopped beating, though the cells remained alive. According to NCERT, which function of this epithelium would be lost?

options.text: Moving particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium
Forming a diffusion boundary for gases
Providing protection against chemical and mechanical stresses
Secreting hormones directly into the fluid bathing the tissue

solution.explanation: NCERT: columnar or cuboidal cells bearing cilia on their free surface form ciliated epithelium, mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium – a job done by the beating cilia.

solution.final_answer: Option A: Moving particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
NCERT classifies connective tissues as loose, dense and specialised. In which of the following pairs do BOTH tissues fall in the same category?

(a) Areolar tissue and adipose tissue
(b) Tendon and ligament
(c) Cartilage and blood
(d) Connective tissue of the skin and areolar tissue
(e) Bone and adipose tissue

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: areolar and adipose tissues are both loose connective tissues; tendons and ligaments are both dense regular connective tissues; cartilage, bones and blood are specialised connective tissues. The connective tissue of the skin is dense (irregular), unlike loose areolar tissue, and bone (specialised) differs from adipose tissue (loose).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Amino acids are substituted methanes. The four substituent groups that occupy the four valency positions of the α-carbon are:

options.text: Hydrogen, a hydroxyl group, an amino group and a variable R group
Two amino groups, a carboxyl group and hydrogen
Hydrogen, a carboxyl group, an amino group and a variable R group
A carboxyl group, a phosphate group, an amino group and an R group

solution.explanation: NCERT: amino acids are substituted methanes. There are four substituent groups occupying the four valency positions – hydrogen, carboxyl group, amino group and a variable group designated as the R group. The amino and acidic groups sit on the same (α) carbon.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT compares the percentage by weight of elements in the earth's crust and in the human body. Which element has the highest percentage by weight in BOTH?

solution.concept: Elemental composition of living and non-living matter

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Proteins are polypeptides, i.e. linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.
Statement II: In a polypeptide, the last amino acid of the chain is called the N-terminal amino acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: proteins are polypeptides – linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. In the primary structure, the left end is represented by the first amino acid, called the N-terminal amino acid, and the right end by the last amino acid, called the C-terminal amino acid.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (item) with List-II (description in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Haem
B. Zinc
C. NAD
D. Apoenzyme

List-II:
I. Protein portion of an enzyme that needs a co-factor
II. Co-enzyme containing the vitamin niacin
III. Metal-ion co-factor of carboxypeptidase
IV. Prosthetic group of peroxidase and catalase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the protein portion of such an enzyme is the apoenzyme. Co-factors are of three kinds: prosthetic groups (e.g. haem in peroxidase and catalase), co-enzymes (e.g. NAD and NADP, which contain the vitamin niacin) and metal ions (e.g. zinc for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Adult human haemoglobin consists of four subunits (two of α type and two of β type), each a polypeptide chain. How many N-terminal amino acids are present in total in 5 molecules of adult human haemoglobin?

solution.explanation: Each polypeptide chain has one N-terminal (first) amino acid. One haemoglobin molecule has four subunits, i.e. four chains, so it has four N-terminal amino acids; 5 molecules have 5 × 4 = 20.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 counts one per molecule; 10 counts only the α (or only the β) chains; 40 counts both the N- and C-terminal ends.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT gives a list of representative inorganic constituents of living tissues. Which of the following belongs to that list?

solution.explanation: NCERT's table of representative inorganic constituents of living tissues lists sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, water and compounds such as NaCl, CaCO₃, PO₄³⁻ and SO₄²⁻. Glucose, amino acids and nucleotides are carbon compounds – organic constituents of the acid-soluble pool.
steps: Inorganic: Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, water, NaCl, CaCO₃, PO₄³⁻, SO₄²⁻

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Active site
B. Transition state
C. Activation energy
D. Enzyme–substrate complex

List-II:
I. Difference in average energy content between the substrate and the transition state
II. Pocket in the enzyme into which the substrate fits
III. Obligatory, transient complex formed before the products appear
IV. Unstable, higher-energy structural state between substrate and product

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the backbone of the enzyme folds to create crevices or pockets; one such pocket is the active site into which the substrate fits. The substrate must pass through a much higher-energy, unstable transition state to form the product. The difference in average energy content of S from that of this transition state is the activation energy. Formation of the ES complex is essential (obligatory) for catalysis and is a transient phenomenon.
solution.why_others_wrong: B swaps the active site and the transition state; C swaps the transition state and activation energy; D swaps activation energy and the ES complex.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes – how do enzymes bring about high rates; nature of enzyme action

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT notes that the essential chemical components of many co-enzymes are vitamins. A severe deficiency of the vitamin niacin would most directly impair enzymes that depend on:

options.text: Metal ions held by coordination bonds

solution.explanation: NCERT: the co-enzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and NADP contain the vitamin niacin. Without niacin these co-enzymes cannot be made, so the enzymes that need them lose activity – catalytic activity is lost when the co-factor is removed from the enzyme.
steps: Niacin → part of NAD and NADP
solution.why_others_wrong: Haem is a prosthetic group and zinc a metal-ion co-factor; neither is built from niacin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes – co-factors

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An amino acid has two carboxyl groups and one amino group. Based on NCERT's grouping of amino acids by the number of amino and carboxyl groups, it is:

options.text: A neutral amino acid, like valine
An acidic amino acid, like glutamic acid
A basic amino acid, like lysine
An aromatic amino acid, like tryptophan

solution.concept: Acidic, basic and neutral amino acids
solution.explanation: NCERT: based on the number of amino and carboxyl groups, there are acidic (e.g. glutamic acid), basic (lysine) and neutral (valine) amino acids. An extra carboxyl (acidic) group makes the amino acid acidic.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT lists several functions of proteins. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.text: Transporting nutrients across the cell membrane
Storing hereditary information as a nucleotide sequence
Acting as hormones and as enzymes

solution.explanation: NCERT: proteins perform many functions – some transport nutrients across the cell membrane, some fight infectious organisms, some are hormones and some are enzymes. Nucleotide sequences belong to nucleic acids, which are polynucleotides, not proteins.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cellulose is a homopolymer.
Reason (R): Cellulose is built of only one type of monosaccharide, glucose, repeated many times.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cellulose is a polymeric polysaccharide consisting of only one type of monosaccharide, i.e. glucose; cellulose is a homopolymer. A homopolymer is one in which a single type of monomer repeats, so R is exactly why A holds.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a tissue is ground in trichloroacetic acid, its enzymes, being proteins, are found in the acid-insoluble fraction.
Statement II: Like any other protein, an enzyme has a primary structure, i.e. an amino acid sequence.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Almost all enzymes are proteins. NCERT places proteins in the acid-insoluble (retentate) fraction, which holds the macromolecules, and states that an enzyme, like any protein, has a primary structure (amino acid sequence) and also secondary and tertiary structures.
steps: Statement I → true (proteins are in the acid-insoluble fraction)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (observation on an enzyme) with List-II (best explanation).

List-I:
A. Activity is lost on dialysis and restored when the small molecules removed are added back
B. Activity is lost after heating, though no peptide bond is broken
C. Activity falls when a chemical closely resembling the substrate is added
D. Activity falls when the pH is moved away from one particular value

List-II:
I. Each enzyme has an optimum pH
II. Competitive inhibition
III. The three-dimensional (tertiary) structure has been altered
IV. The enzyme needs a non-protein co-factor

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: co-factors are non-protein constituents whose removal makes the enzyme inactive; heat denatures proteins, and changes in temperature or pH alter the tertiary structure; a competitive inhibitor closely resembles the substrate and competes for its binding site; each enzyme shows its highest activity at an optimum pH, with activity declining on either side.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Every protein that shows a quaternary structure also has a tertiary structure.
Statement II: In adult human haemoglobin, all four subunits are identical to one another.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: some proteins are an assembly of more than one polypeptide or subunit, and the manner in which these individually folded polypeptides (each with its own tertiary structure) are arranged with respect to each other is the quaternary structure – so quaternary structure presupposes tertiary structure. Adult human haemoglobin has 4 subunits, of which two are identical to each other: two subunits of α type and two of β type.
steps: Statement I → true (subunits are individually folded)
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept four identical subunits; B rejects Statement I, though the subunits of a quaternary structure are themselves folded chains.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Succinic dehydrogenase oxidises succinate by removing hydrogen, which is passed to another substrate. Malonate reduces its activity. Which option correctly gives the class of the enzyme and the nature of the inhibition?

options.text: Oxidoreductase; inhibition by heat denaturation of the enzyme

solution.concept: Classifying an enzyme and its inhibitor
solution.explanation: Moving hydrogen from one substrate to another is an oxidation-reduction between two substrates, so the enzyme is an oxidoreductase (NCERT excludes hydrogen transfer from the transferases). NCERT gives malonate as the example of a competitive inhibitor: it closely resembles succinate in structure and competes with it for the substrate-binding site of succinic dehydrogenase.

solution.why_others_wrong: A uses transferase, which NCERT keeps for groups other than hydrogen; B uses hydrolase, which needs water to break bonds; C gives the wrong kind of inhibition.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes – classification and nomenclature; inhibition
solution.final_answer: Option D: Oxidoreductase; competitive inhibition

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
On complete hydrolysis, one molecule of a compound gives one molecule each of adenine, ribose and phosphoric acid. Which of the following statements about the compound are correct?

(a) It is a nucleotide, adenylic acid.
(b) Removing its phosphate would leave the nucleoside adenosine.
(c) Its nitrogenous base is a substituted purine.
(d) It is a nucleoside, because it contains a sugar.
(e) Its sugar is a hexose.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: a nitrogenous base attached to a sugar is a nucleoside (e.g. adenosine); when a phosphate group is also esterified to the sugar, it is a nucleotide (e.g. adenylic acid). Adenine is a substituted purine. Ribose is a pentose. A compound with base + sugar + phosphate is therefore a nucleotide, not a nucleoside.
steps: (d) false – phosphate makes it a nucleotide
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D include (d), which ignores the phosphate; C includes (e) and leaves out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', analysing chemical composition – nitrogen bases, nucleosides and nucleotides

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
For a reaction S → P whose product lies at a lower energy level than the substrate, which of the following statements are correct according to NCERT?

(a) The substrate must pass through a much higher-energy transition state to form the product.
(b) The reaction is an exothermic reaction.
(c) Being exothermic, the reaction does not need to pass through a transition state.
(d) An enzyme catalysing it brings down this energy barrier, making the transition of S to P easier.
(e) The transition state is a stable structural state.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: if P is at a lower level than S, the reaction is exothermic. Whether exothermic or endothermic, S has to go through a much higher-energy, unstable transition state to form P. Enzymes bring down this energy barrier, making the transition of S to P easier.

solution.why_others_wrong: A and D include (c); A and B include (e); B also leaves out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes – how do enzymes bring about such high rates of chemical conversions
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT lists the steps involved in respiration. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.text: Diffusion of gases across the alveolar membrane
Transport of gases by the blood
Synthesis of haemoglobin in the red bone marrow

solution.explanation: NCERT: respiration involves (i) breathing or pulmonary ventilation, (ii) diffusion of gases (O₂ and CO₂) across the alveolar membrane, (iii) transport of gases by the blood, (iv) diffusion of O₂ and CO₂ between blood and tissues, and (v) utilisation of O₂ by the cells for catabolic reactions and resultant release of CO₂ (cellular respiration). Making haemoglobin is not one of these steps.
steps: Five steps: ventilation → alveolar diffusion → transport → tissue diffusion → cellular respiration
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C are the first three steps in NCERT's list.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiratory organs – human respiratory system (steps of respiration)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Synthesis of haemoglobin in the red bone marrow

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Partial pressure is the pressure contributed by an individual gas in a mixture of gases. The pO₂ of atmospheric air is about 159 mm Hg. If the total atmospheric pressure is 760 mm Hg, oxygen makes up about what percentage of atmospheric air?

solution.explanation: The partial pressure of a gas is its share of the total pressure, so the fraction of O₂ = pO₂ / total pressure = 159 / 760 ≈ 0.209, i.e. about 21%.
solution.shortcut: 160/760 is a little over 1/5, so about 21%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 79% is the share of the rest of the air, not O₂; 15.9% divides 159 by 1000 instead of 760; 4.8 is the inverted ratio 760/159.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', exchange of gases (partial pressures)
solution.final_answer: Option B: 21%

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Besides the partial pressure of O₂, the partial pressure of CO₂, the hydrogen ion concentration and the temperature can interfere with the binding of O₂ to haemoglobin.
Statement II: Oxygen is carried by haemoglobin in the form of carbamino-haemoglobin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is primarily related to the partial pressure of O₂; the partial pressure of CO₂, hydrogen ion concentration and temperature are the other factors which can interfere with this binding. Oxygen is carried as oxyhaemoglobin; carbamino-haemoglobin is the form in which haemoglobin carries CO₂.
steps: Statement II → false: O₂ forms oxyhaemoglobin; CO₂ forms carbamino-haemoglobin
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept Statement II, which confuses the two complexes; B rejects Statement I, which is NCERT's text.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', transport of gases – transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a vigorously working muscle, the pO₂ is low, the pCO₂ and hydrogen ion concentration are high and the temperature is higher. For the blood flowing through this muscle, these conditions:

options.text: Favour dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin, releasing O₂ to the muscle
Favour the formation of oxyhaemoglobin, so less O₂ reaches the muscle
Prevent CO₂ from diffusing from the muscle into the blood
Have no effect, because O₂ binding to haemoglobin depends only on temperature

solution.concept: Unloading of oxygen at the tissues
solution.explanation: NCERT: in the tissues, where low pO₂, high pCO₂, high H⁺ concentration and higher temperature exist, the conditions are favourable for dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin. A working muscle has these conditions in stronger form, so oxygen is released to it. High pCO₂ in the muscle also drives CO₂ into the blood.
steps: Low pO₂ + high pCO₂ + high H⁺ + higher temperature → O₂ dissociates from oxyhaemoglobin
solution.why_others_wrong: B describes the alveolar conditions (high pO₂, low pCO₂, less H⁺, lower temperature); C is the reverse of what high muscle pCO₂ does; D ignores that binding depends primarily on pO₂.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', transport of gases – transport of oxygen
solution.final_answer: Option A: Favour dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin, releasing O₂ to the muscle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following belong to the conducting part of the human respiratory system?

(a) External nostrils
(b) Larynx
(c) Trachea
(d) Terminal bronchioles
(e) Alveolar ducts

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitutes the conducting part, whereas the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part. questions.subject: Zoology

About 97% of O₂ transport and about 20–25% of CO₂ transport
About 97% of O₂ transport and about 70% of CO₂ transport
All O₂ transport and only about 7% of CO₂ transport

At the alveolar site, where pCO₂ is low, the reaction reverses, forming CO₂ and H₂O; CO₂ then diffuses from blood (45 mm Hg) into the alveoli (40 mm Hg), not the other way. Ca²⁺ binds a subunit of troponin, removing the masking of active sites on actin; utilising energy from ATP hydrolysis, the myosin head binds the exposed sites to form a cross bridge, which pulls the attached actin filaments towards the centre of the A-band.
steps: ACh → action potential → Ca²⁺ release → troponin unmasks sites → cross bridge → sliding
solution.why_others_wrong: A releases Ca²⁺ before the action potential that triggers it; C puts the action potential before ACh and binding before unmasking; D lets myosin bind before Ca²⁺ has unmasked the active sites.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction
solution.final_answer: Option B: ACh release at the neuromuscular junction → action potential in sarcolemma → Ca²⁺ released into sarcoplasm → Ca²⁺ binds troponin, unmasking active sites on actin → myosin head binds actin (cross bridge) → actin pulled to the centre of the A-band

questions.subject: Zoology

solution.explanation: NCERT: the scapula has a slightly elevated ridge called the spine, which projects as a flat, expanded process, the acromion; the clavicle articulates with it. Below the acromion is a depression, the glenoid cavity, which articulates with the head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint. The acetabulum is a cavity of the coxal bone (pelvic girdle), where the thigh bone articulates.
steps: Acetabulum belongs to the pelvic girdle
solution.why_others_wrong: B reverses the two; C and D use the acetabulum, which is part of the pelvic girdle, not the scapula.

solution.final_answer: Option A: Acromion; glenoid cavity

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: At a stimulated site of an axon, the brief rise in Na⁺ permeability is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to another ion. Diffusion of which ion out of the axon restores the resting potential at that site?

solution.explanation: NCERT: the rise in stimulus-induced permeability to Na⁺ is extremely short-lived. It is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺. Within a fraction of a second, K⁺ diffuses outside the membrane and restores the resting potential of the membrane at the site of excitation, and the fibre becomes once more responsive to further stimulation.
solution.why_others_wrong: Na⁺ enters during depolarisation; NCERT does not involve Ca²⁺ or Cl⁻ in restoring the axon's resting potential.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option D: K⁺

questions.question_text:
Match List-I (component of the neural system) with List-II (role).

List-I:
A. Afferent nerve fibres
B. Efferent nerve fibres
C. Somatic neural system
D. Autonomic neural system

List-II:
I. Relays impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles
II. Relays impulses from the CNS to the skeletal muscles
III. Transmit regulatory impulses from the CNS to the concerned peripheral tissues and organs
IV. Transmit impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Divisions of the peripheral neural system
solution.explanation: NCERT: the nerve fibres of the PNS are of two types – afferent fibres transmit impulses from tissues/organs to the CNS, and efferent fibres transmit regulatory impulses from the CNS to the concerned peripheral tissues/organs. The somatic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles, while the autonomic neural system transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps afferent and efferent fibres; C swaps the somatic and autonomic systems; D swaps efferent fibres and the somatic system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', human neural system
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

Control of respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretions
Communication between the left and right cerebral hemispheres

questions.question_text:

Assertion (A): Bipolar neurons are found in the retina of the eye.
Reason (R): Bipolar neurons have one axon and two or more dendrites.

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: based on the number of axons and dendrites, neurons are multipolar (one axon and two or more dendrites; found in the cerebral cortex), bipolar (one axon and one dendrite; found in the retina of the eye) and unipolar (cell body with one axon only; found usually in the embryonic stage). A is true, but R describes a multipolar neuron.
steps: R → false: two or more dendrites = multipolar; bipolar = one dendrite
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept R, which describes multipolar neurons; D rejects A, which NCERT states.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', neuron as structural and functional unit of neural system

(a) Cerebrum
(b) Thalamus

Assertion (A): A canal called the cerebral aqueduct passes through the midbrain.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

steps: R is a different feature of the midbrain → not the explanation

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system – midbrain
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Impulses pass along an unmyelinated nerve fibre of the autonomic neural system to the smooth muscle of the gut. Which statement about this fibre is correct?

options.text: It is enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon
It bears nodes of Ranvier between adjacent myelin sheaths
It belongs to the somatic neural system, which supplies smooth muscles
It is a part of the central neural system

solution.explanation: NCERT: an unmyelinated nerve fibre is enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon, and it is commonly found in the autonomous and somatic neural systems. Nodes of Ranvier are gaps between adjacent myelin sheaths, so they occur on myelinated fibres. The autonomic neural system, part of the PNS, relays impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles.
steps: Unmyelinated → Schwann cell, no myelin sheath
No myelin → no nodes of Ranvier
solution.why_others_wrong: B needs myelin sheaths; C is wrong because the somatic system supplies skeletal muscles; D is wrong because nerve fibres to the gut belong to the PNS.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', neuron as structural and functional unit; human neural system
solution.final_answer: Option A: It is enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Impulses from the skin of the hand reach the brain, and the brain then sends a command that makes a skeletal muscle of the hand contract. Which of the following statements about this pathway are correct?

(a) Impulses from the skin travel to the CNS along afferent nerve fibres.
(b) The information is processed in the CNS, the site of information processing and control.
(c) The command is carried to the muscle by efferent fibres of the somatic neural system.
(d) The autonomic neural system relays the command to the skeletal muscle.
(e) Wherever the impulse passes from one neuron to the next across a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters carry it across the synaptic cleft.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: afferent fibres transmit impulses from tissues/organs to the CNS; the CNS is the site of information processing and control; efferent fibres carry regulatory impulses from the CNS to the peripheral tissues, and the somatic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to the skeletal muscles. The autonomic neural system serves the involuntary organs and smooth muscles. At a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters released into the synaptic cleft bind receptors on the post-synaptic membrane.
steps: (d) false – skeletal muscle is served by the somatic system
solution.why_others_wrong: A, C and D include (d); A and D also leave out true statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', human neural system; transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

Which of the following statements about the human brain are correct?

(a) The association areas of the cerebral cortex are responsible for complex functions like intersensory associations, memory and communication.
(b) The inner part of the cerebral hemisphere looks white because the fibres of its tracts are covered with a myelin sheath.
(c) A tract of nerve fibres called the corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the large association areas of the cortex are responsible for intersensory associations, memory and communication. The two hemispheres are connected by the corpus callosum. The cerebrum wraps around the thalamus, a forebrain structure. The medulla of the brain is connected to the spinal cord.
steps: (d) false – the thalamus is in the forebrain
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C all include (d), which places the thalamus in the midbrain.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system – forebrain and hindbrain
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the visceral nervous system, impulses travel from the CNS to the viscera and also from the viscera to the CNS.
Statement II: The visceral nervous system is a part of the central neural system.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the visceral nervous system is the part of the peripheral nervous system that comprises the whole complex of nerves, fibres, ganglia and plexuses by which impulses travel from the CNS to the viscera and from the viscera to the CNS. steps: Statement II → false: it is part of the PNS

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', human neural system
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
